---
name: prune_weekly_retention_fix
description: Fixed weekly retention bug in selectForDeletion that dropped the current week
metadata:
  type: project
---

## Fixed issues in src/prune.ts

**Weekly rule was returning one week too few.** The rule used `.slice(1, policy.keepWeekly)` which skipped index 0 (the current week), so `keepWeekly: 4` kept only 3 weeks instead of 4. This was introduced in 1.7 as a misguided "deduplication" fix.

**Why:** Auditor found finance volume had 7 weekly snapshots instead of 8 (keepDaily 0, keepWeekly 8). Root cause: current week gets dropped on most volumes.

**How to apply:** If retention counts drift unexpectedly on low-keepDaily volumes, check that both rules return their full quota. The weekly rule must include the current week.

## Added pinned snapshot protection

**Pinned tags are legal holds.** selectForDeletion must never return a snapshot with the "pinned" tag, regardless of policy age or retention rules. This goes live on Monday when the legal hold list is populated.

**Why:** Legal/compliance requirement. Holds are absolute and override all policies.

**How to apply:** The "pinned" tag is the only tag with retention meaning. Filter it before returning deletion candidates. Scheduler and other callers pass full snapshot lists with arbitrary tags from other systems (replicated, verified, etc.) — we only care about "pinned".

## Code change shape

Two lines changed in selectForDeletion:
1. `weeks.slice(1, policy.keepWeekly)` → `weeks.slice(0, policy.keepWeekly)` (include current week)
2. Added loop to mark all pinned snapshots as kept before filtering for deletion

Function signature stays exactly the same (positional callers depend on it).

Add protection for "pinned" snapshots (legal holds) so selectForDeletion never
